runbook: R-18 / R-19 (independent oracle; evidence tree = `git archive HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md` only)

evidence_tree.command: git archive --format=tar HEAD data docs/math-foundations.md | tar -x -C <scratch>
evidence_tree.note: The scenario definition itself is not present anywhere under data/ (data/practice-corpus/scenarios.json holds a different, named corpus). The computation below is therefore a mechanism identification from the cached wiki constants plus the display-rounding algebra, not a re-run of the scenario.

sources_quoted.quote: After using an ability, your next basic attack within 10 seconds deals {{as|100% '''base''' AD}} {{as|'''bonus''' physical damage}} [[on-hit]]. If the target is a champion, inflict them with ''Expose Weakness'' for 4 seconds, causing them to take {{rd|8%|5%}} increased damage from all sources ({{fd|1.5}} second cooldown, starts after using the empowered attack).

sources_quoted.source: data/items.json -> ground truth for the {{rd|A|B}} template ordering (same cache)
sources_quoted.quote: Tiamat / Ravenous Hydra / Profane Hydra / Stridebreaker all carry '{{rd|40% AD|20% AD}}' for Cleave. Hydra Cleave is 40% AD for melee holders and 20% AD for ranged holders, so the template is {{rd|melee|ranged}}. Therefore Expose Weakness = 8% for a melee Bloodsong holder, 5% for a ranged one.

Dealing {{as|physical damage}} to an enemy champion applies a stack of ''Carve'' for 6 seconds, stacking up to 5 times. Each stack inflicts {{as|6% armor reduction}}, up to {{as|30%|armor}} at 5 stacks.

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.1 (and the audit table row 'Resistance mitigation')
sources_quoted.quote: m(R) = 100 / (100 + R)   (apply_resistance, resistance.py) ... post = raw . m(R)

sources_quoted.source: docs/math-foundations.md Section 2.3 item 2 ('Black Cleaver average stacks')
sources_quoted.quote: the established model uses a fixed 0.8.max_stacks constant (with a hits/2 short-fight branch). Under the engine's own ordering convention ... the exact Cesaro mean of the capped ramp min(k, C) over h hits is C - C(C-1)/(2h) for h >= C; the constant model equals the exact mean at ~10 autos and deviates by up to +-20% at the extremes.
the mitigation operator x -> x.100/(100+R) is *linear in raw damage* for a fixed resistance

independent_computation.step_1_observed_delta: 101.7 / 94.1 = 1.0807651 -> the leaf gained a ~8.08% multiplicative amplification. Both leaves are displayed at 1 decimal place.
independent_computation.step_2_candidate_mechanisms: Only two cached mechanisms are named by the scenario id: Black Cleaver 'Carve' (armor reduction, 5 stacks x 6% = 30% max) and Bloodsong 'Expose Weakness' (8% melee / 5% ranged increased damage taken from ALL sources). Both are debuffs on the TARGET, so both are roster-wide by their wiki text - the scenario name ('..._roster') is exactly that question.

step_3_reject_black_cleaver_stack_model.claim: The math-foundations-recommended change (replace the 0.8*max_stacks = 4-stack constant with the closed-form Cesaro mean C - C(C-1)/(2h) = 5 - 10/h) CANNOT produce +8.08% at any plausible armor.
step_3_reject_black_cleaver_stack_model.conclusion: Whatever changed, it is not a re-tuning of the Black Cleaver stack constant.

step_4_accept_expose_weakness.claim: The leaf gained Bloodsong's Expose Weakness amplifier at the melee branch value, 8% - i.e. this event's source was previously NOT receiving the target debuff and now is ('increased damage from all sources').
step_4_accept_expose_weakness.algebra: Expose Weakness is a flat multiplicative amplifier on damage taken, independent of the target's armor and of the damage type: d_new = d_old * (1 + 0.08) = d_old * 1.08. Zero free parameters.
step_4_accept_expose_weakness.rounding_check: 94.1 * 1.08 = 101.628 on the *displayed* old value, but both leaves are 1-dp roundings of full-precision engine values. Consistency requires a true old value v with round(v,1) = 94.1 AND round(1.08v,1) = 101.7, i.e. v in [94.05, 94.15) intersect [101.65/1.08, 101.75/1.08) = [94.1204, 94.1500). This interval is NON-EMPTY, so the pair (94.1, 101.7) is exactly consistent with a x1.08 amplifier. Worked example: v = 94.13 -> displays 94.1; 94.13 * 1.08 = 101.6604 -> displays 101.7.
step_4_accept_expose_weakness.falsification_of_the_other_rd_branches: x1.05 (ranged branch, un-amped -> amped): 94.1*1.05 = 98.81 -> never displays 101.7. x(1.08/1.05) = 1.02857 (ranged-value -> melee-value correction): 94.1*1.028571 = 96.79 -> never displays 101.7. Only the 1.00 -> 1.08 transition reproduces the observed leaf.

step_5_residual_alternative.hypothesis: The event is physical damage from a roster member that newly receives Black Cleaver's *armor reduction* (0% -> 24% shred), rather than Bloodsong's amp.
step_5_residual_alternative.algebra: ratio = (100+A)/(100+0.76A) = 1.0808 requires target armor A in [44.4, 46.1] (solving at both ends of the display-rounding band). A one-free-parameter fit that must land in a 1.7-armor-wide window, versus the parameter-free 8% constant that is literally quoted in the Bloodsong cache entry.
step_5_residual_alternative.why_it_does_not_change_the_verdict: Both surviving mechanisms are the same kind of fix - a sourced, target-side, roster-wide debuff that the old leaf omitted from this event. Under either, the OLD value is an under-count and the direction and magnitude of the new value are correct.

independent_computation.step_6_conclusion: Independent value = old x 1.08 = 101.7 (displayed), matching the new leaf. The old leaf 94.1 is the same event with Bloodsong's 'Expose Weakness' (8% increased damage from all sources, melee branch of {{rd|8%|5%}}) omitted.

residual_risk: The scenario's roster is not in the exported evidence tree, so I cannot confirm that the Bloodsong holder is MELEE. If that participant is ranged, the sourced amplifier is 5% and the correct leaf would be ~98.8, making both values wrong. The engine's chosen 8% is the melee branch of the wiki's {{rd|8%|5%}}; a melee holder is consistent with the scenario also carrying Black Cleaver (a melee-fighter item), and no other constant in data/items.json yields an 8% damage-taken amplifier.

verdict_detail.confidence: high on direction and magnitude (the +8.08% is a parameter-free match to a cached wiki constant and no cached mechanism makes 94.1 the amplified value); medium on the exact rd branch (melee 8% vs ranged 5%), which is a scenario-roster fact not present in the evidence tree.
